grievance: Asking zot for help failed. `zot --help` and `zot -h` fell through to pflag's built-in handling: the usage block was dumped on stderr, a stray `pflag: help requested` line was printed on stdout, and the exit status was 2 - so `zot --help | less` showed one useless line, redirecting help to a file captured nothing useful, and anything scripting around the command saw it fail. The subcommands fared no better: `zot new --help`, `zot sessions --help` and `zot sessions export --help` each ended in an error (status 1) with only an auto-generated flag dump on stderr. The first command anyone runs against a new tool was broken.
change: Help is now a real flag on every surface that takes one: `-h/--help` at the top level and on `new`, `sessions` and `sessions export`. Asking for help prints the usage to stdout and exits 0, before any validation or filesystem work (`zot new --provider x --help` answers with help instead of refusing, and scaffolds nothing). `usage()` takes its destination writer, so one help text serves both audiences - stdout when asked for, stderr from the error paths, which are otherwise unchanged (an unknown flag still explains itself on stderr with a non-zero status). Subcommand usage blocks became writer-parameterised closures rendering FlagUsages(), dropping pflag's global-output mutation.
proof: Observed before the change: `./zot --help >o 2>e` left o containing exactly 'pflag: help requested' (22 bytes), e holding the 4,805-byte usage, status 2; `./zot new --help` exited 1 with stdout empty. Observed after rebuilding: `./zot --help` exits 0 with the full 4,858 bytes of usage on stdout and zero bytes on stderr (`grep -c pflag` finds none); `-h`, `zot new --help`, `zot sessions --help`/`-h` and `zot sessions export --help`/`-h` each print their usage on stdout with status 0; `./zot --nope` still prints 'unknown flag' plus usage on stderr and exits 2; `zot new --provider x fix the typo` still refuses; and a work order run against a local stub provider still ends settled with the full digest block (session id, resume line, token counts). The five new tests (TestRunHelpIsAnsweredOnStdout, TestRunHelpBeatsTheRestOfTheCommandLine, TestNewOrderHelpAnswersWithoutScaffolding, TestListSessionsHelpAndErrorsGoToDifferentStreams, TestExportSessionsHelpAndErrorsGoToDifferentStreams) were bite-checked: with main.go reverted to d33ccbe all five fail; with the change they pass. Gate green afterwards: make vet over both build variants, full make test, make cover-check at 91.8% (threshold 90%).

grievance: Listing a session history read every log back whole. session.List - behind `zot sessions`, behind --resume last, and behind the automatic continuation check that every single order dispatch performs - loaded each .jsonl in full, decoding every message text and every captured tool output into memory only to discard all of it but the task line and the outcome. A project run unattended accumulates one log per run forever, so the cost of starting any order climbed with everything ever run: measured against a directory of 600 logs (~190 MB), each order dispatch paid ~1.2 s before its first provider call (0.18 s -> 1.34-1.69 s), `zot sessions` took 1.24 s, and both scale linearly - months of a standing order turn into minutes paid on every dispatch, and watch mode pays it per picked-up order.
change: List now scans instead of loading. A new scanEntry streams each log line by line and reads only what a listing shows: the meta record's task and provenance, whether a result closed the run, and that result's reason. The kind is read off the head of each line without decoding it (kindOf) - this package's writer emits kind first - so message/event/reset lines, where all the bytes live, never reach encoding/json at all; Unmarshal's own skipping still walks every skipped byte, so avoiding the call entirely was worth ~16x on its own. Any line whose kind cannot be read off its head is decoded whole through listingRecord, so a hand-edited or third-party log lists exactly as before, and unreadable files and half-written final lines are skipped precisely as Load's callers did. Load, resume, export and receipts are untouched - they still read conversations in full.
proof: Rebuilt and ran the binary against a synthetic factory directory (600 logs, ~190 MB) plus one deliberately reformatted log. Before: `zot sessions` 1.24 s / ~20 MB RSS; an order dispatch through --rerun took 0.18 s with a small session dir and 1.34-1.69 s pointed at the big one. After: `zot sessions` 0.07 s, dispatch 0.18-0.27 s - the history tax is gone - and `--resume last` still runs to settled against the big directory. The new listing's output is identical: the 600 'factory shift' rows diff clean against the pre-change listing, and the reformatted log (keys reordered, spaces after colons, kind not first) lists correctly through the fallback as failed/aborted. In-repo benchmark: BenchmarkListOverHistory 21.6 ms/op vs BenchmarkLoadOverHistory 752 ms/op (~35x). Tests added (internal/session/listing_test.go): TestListMatchesAFullRead pins List against full-read entries across concluded/failed/unfinished/resumed/reset/truncated/reformatted shapes; TestKindOfReadsTheKindOffTheHead covers writer-shaped heads and every unknown-shape fallback; TestListDoesNotDecodePayloadsWhileListing fails if a listing ever goes back to reading logs whole (bite-checked by reverting List to Load-based derivation: 6.3 MB allocated vs the 2.3 MB ceiling); TestListStartedIsTheFileTime pins Started to the mod time. Gate green afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, full make test, make cover-check at 91.9%

grievance: `zot sessions` - the one place an operator reads a night of unattended runs - showed only a session id (a UTC timestamp needing decoding), a stop-reason word, and sixty characters of task text. Everything else a run records about its own ending had to be pried out of files by hand: how long the run went, and what it cost in provider-billed tokens - numbers the end-of-run digest prints and the ledger receipt keeps, but which vanished in the index over them. Answering "what did last night's shifts cost me?" meant piping every .jsonl through jq; and since all sessions share one global directory across projects, there was not even a per-project shortcut. The tool whose whole premise is that unattended runs leave answerable records made you open each log to answer the two questions asked most often.
change: Each row now reads <id> <status> <length> <in/out> <task>: the run's length from its meta record to its result record rendered compactly (38s / 4m40s / 1h06m, sub-second as <1s), and the billed totals in the digest's own shape (15.4k/4.2k). Absence is stated as a dash, never a confident zero - an unfinished run has no length or cost to state, and a log written before the token fields existed is unrecorded rather than free. session.Entry grew Ended/Duration/InputTokens/OutputTokens, lifted in scanEntry from the very same two small meta/result lines the shift-2 scanner already decodes - listingRecord just carries `at` now - so message and event payloads still never reach the decoder, dispatch-time continuation checks pay nothing extra, Started stays the file's mod time exactly as pinned before, and the allocation-ceiling test still holds the scan's cost to the number of runs rather than their size.
proof: Ran the rebuilt binary against a local stub provider that reports usage and takes wall-clock time. The digest of a real order run printed input-tokens 15432 / output-tokens 4211; `./zot sessions` showed that run as `20260826-053734  settled  7s  15.4k/4.2k  second task` - length and cost matching the digest, where the pre-shift binary printed `20260826-053734 ... settled  second task` with no numbers at all. Runs whose logs record no usage show `-` and sub-second stub runs show `<1s`: absence stated as absence. A killed mid-flight log lists as running/interrupted with dashes, and `zot sessions export`, bare dispatch, watch pickup and auto-continue are unaffected (fields are additive). Tests: TestListLiftsWhatTheResultRecords pins ended/duration/tokens for a concluded log and all-zero for an unfinished one; TestListMatchesAFullRead now also holds the fast listing to full-read parity on the new fields across concluded/resumed/reformatted/truncated shapes; TestListSessionsShowsHowLongAndWhatItCost asserts the rendered columns including the dashes; TestSessionListingCellFormatting pins the cell rules (<1s, 1m00s, 4m40s, 1h06m, dash, 12.3k/678 compaction). Bite-checked by removing the lift from scanEntry: parity and lift tests fail on exactly the new fields; restored, they pass. Gate green afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, make test, make cover-check at 91.9% (threshold 90%).

grievance: A custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint was handed Responses-API requests it never agreed to speak. The wire format was inferred from the driver and the model alone (wantsResponses): any connection with driver openai carrying a model the catalogue marks as reasoning - including zot's own default, glm-5.2 - sent POST <base_url>/responses even when base_url pointed at a gateway or self-hosted deployment implementing only chat-completions. That contradicted zot's own documented rule (docs/providers.md: 'Only OpenAI implements it today, so everywhere else stays on chat-completions') and failed in the worst way: the run started fine, then died on its first turn with 'provider: 404 page not found (404)' - no hint the wrong API had been spoken, no configuration to say otherwise (the existing DisableResponses flag was unreachable from YAML), so the front-door setup README advertises ('any OpenAI-compatible provider... a gateway, a custom endpoint') with the default model was broken out of the box.
change: Automatic Responses selection now applies only to OpenAI's own built-in endpoint: wantsResponses takes the override decision Resolve already computed and returns false when the endpoint was overridden (explicit UseResponses/DisableResponses still win, so an operator who knows better is obeyed). The choice became configurable end to end: providers take a tri-state `responses:` field in YAML (true forces Responses, false forces chat-completions, unset is automatic), carried through config.ProviderConfig.Responses -> agent.ClientOptions.Responses (mapped onto provider.Config.UseResponses/DisableResponses in NewClient) -> zot.resolve(), which every run of record and every drafting survey goes through. agent.Client gained UsesResponses() exposing the resolved answer beside Model()/Provider()/BaseURL(). One existing test (TestResponsesSendsMaxOutputTokens) had silently depended on the bug - its captureBody helper overrides base_url and the old rule still picked Responses - and now states its intent by forcing UseResponses.
proof: Exercised with a local OpenAI-compatible stub (httptest-shaped SSE) and config `gw: driver openai, base_url http://127.0.0.1:8099/v1, api_key ...`, model glm-5.2. Before the change: six consecutive runs (sessions 20260826-055101 through 055502) died on their first turn - plain output 'failed (code 1): the provider failed', stderr 'zot: provider: 404 page not found (404)', each session log's result recording {reason:error, failure:{status:404, response_body:'404 page not found'}}; the workaround needed was a config-side reasoning:false capability lie. After rebuilding: the same config minus the workaround runs to 'done' (iterations 2, calls 1) and the stub's access log shows only 'POST /v1/chat/completions'; the ledger receipt lands with evidence (session, summary, token totals). Knob proof both directions: adding `responses: true` sent the request to /v1/responses - the stub 404s that path and the new session recorded status 404/'404 page not found' again - so the flag demonstrably flips the wire. Tests: TestResponsesIsSelectedForReasoningModelsOnOpenAI gains 'an OpenAI reasoning model on an overridden endpoint' (want false); TestAnOverriddenEndpointIsSpokenToInChatCompletions drives a real request at a local server with glm-5.2 and fails if any path other than /chat/completions is hit; TestProviderResponsesParsesAsATriState pins yaml responses unset/true/false; TestResolveCarriesTheResponsesChoice and TestAResponsesOptOutReachesOpenAIIself prove file->client threading through resolve() in both directions. Bite-checked: reverting wantsResponses to drop the override check fails the table case (UseResponses = true, want false) and the wire test ('the run sent /responses to an overridden endpoint; want chat-completions'); restored, all pass. No earlier pass's behaviour regressed: sessions listing columns, scan-based listing and help-on-stdout re-exercised during this shift's runs and the full suite passes. Gate green afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, make test, make race, make cover-check at 91.6% (threshold 90%).

grievance: `zot sessions` - the one place an operator reads a night of unattended runs - could say THAT a run ended badly but not WHY. A provider failure rendered as `20260826-083615  error  3s  -  create the file done.txt Acceptance criteria…`: the status word named the category, and the actual cause ('provider: upstream exploded (500)') stayed locked in the run's .jsonl, one hand-run jq per failed order away. The docs sell the log as what turns 'it failed overnight' into something answerable, yet for the most common overnight question - which of these runs died, and of what - the listing still made you open every file. Shift 3 gave the listing length and cost; how each run explained its own ending was the remaining gap, and it was free: the shift-2 scanner already decodes exactly the result record that carries those words.
change: session.Entry grew Outcome - how the run itself explained its ending: the underlying error when it recorded one, otherwise its closing message (the loop's 'the provider failed' names nothing; the provider's own words name the cause) - lifted in scanEntry from the same small result line the scanner already decoded for reason, length and cost, so message payloads still never reach encoding/json and the allocation ceiling is untouched. `zot sessions` quotes that line at the end of the row after an em-dash, rune-safely bounded at 100 characters, but only for endings that need explaining: any concluded run whose reason is neither settled nor stop. A settled row stays just the brief - its summary already reached the operator in the end-of-run digest and the ledger receipt - and a run that never concluded still shows dashes rather than inventing an ending.
proof: Rebuilt the release binary and re-listed the session history produced by this shift's own stub-provider runs. Before: `20260826-083615  error  3s  -  create the file done.txt Acceptance criteria - the objectiv…` with no hint of cause. After: the same rows read `…Acceptance criteria - the objectiv… — provider: upstream exploded (500)` and `— provider: Post "http://127.0.0.1:8124/v1/chat/completions": dial tcp …` (rune-bounded ellipsis), while every settled row is byte-identical to before and the killed-mid-flight run (`running/interrupted`) still shows dashes with no suffix. A fresh order dispatched against the always-500 stub then listed its own ending as `20260826-090348  error  3s  -  demonstrate the sessions listing — provider: upstream exploded (500)` end to end. No earlier pass regressed: help-on-stdout, the listing's length/cost columns and the responses wire choice were all re-exercised during the runs; TestListMatchesAFullRead now holds the fast listing to full-read parity on Outcome across concluded/resumed/reformatted/truncated shapes; BenchmarkListOverHistory is unchanged at ~14.7 ms/op vs 623 ms/op for Load (~42x). Tests added: TestListLiftsHowTheRunExplainedItsEnding (error preferred over the boilerplate message, message-only endings quoted verbatim, guard stops carry their limit, unfinished and wordless endings lift empty) and TestListSessionsSaysWhyARunEnded (failed row quotes its cause; a settled row never grows the suffix; the unfinished row shows no dash-quote). Bite-checked in both layers: removing the scanEntry lift fails both tests; removing only taskColumn's suffix fails the cmd test while the session test still passes; restored, all green. Gate afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, full make test, make race, make cover-check at 91.7% (threshold 90%).

grievance: The automatic continuation of an unfinished run matched sessions by task text alone, while the default session directory is global across every project. Two projects whose orders render the same objective - a standing 'keep the fleet healthy overnight' in each, say - continued each other's interrupted runs: project B's dispatch resumed project A's half-done conversation (announced in B as 'continuing unfinished run <A's id> of this order'), so the agent worked B's tree while believing it had already done A's first half, replaying foreign tool calls and results into the thread. The session log records which directory a run operated in; the one check that most needed that fact never read it.
change: session.Entry now carries Workdir - how the run's meta record answers 'where did this happen' - lifted in scanEntry from the same tiny meta line the shift-2 scanner already decodes for task and provenance, so message payloads still never reach the decoder and the allocation ceiling is untouched. unfinishedRunOf takes the directory the new run operates in (resolved after the chdir into --dir, carried on oneRun and through newWatchRunner) and continues only a session whose recorded workdir equals it: another project's interrupted run neither resumes nor blocks the search, which walks on to this project's own newest interruption. A log recording no workdir belongs to no provable project and is never continued on faith. Explicit --resume is untouched, and the continuation message is unchanged.
proof: Demonstrated end to end with two scratch projects sharing one --session-dir, identical objective text, and a stub provider that accepts the request then hangs. Before the change: project A's run SIGKILLed mid-flight left log 20260826-093153 (workdir projA); bare zot in project B printed 'zot: continuing unfinished run 20260826-093153 of this order (--fresh to start over)' and B's new log recorded resumedFrom 20260826-093153 while working in /tmp/zotscratch/projB - the wrong project's conversation resumed into B's tree. After rebuilding: bare zot in B started its own fresh run (no continuation line; meta resumedFrom empty), while project A's own rerun still announced 'continuing unfinished run 20260826-094902 of this order' and its log carries resumedFrom 20260826-094902 - same-project continuation exactly as before; `zot sessions` rows unchanged in shape (length/cost columns and outcome quoting from shifts 3 and 5 intact), and BenchmarkListOverHistory is unchanged at ~18 ms/op vs ~805 ms/op for Load. Tests added: TestAnUnfinishedRunOfAnotherProjectIsNotContinued (a foreign workdir or no workdir is skipped, this project's older interruption is still found), TestListLiftsWhereTheRunRan, TestListMatchesAFullRead extended to hold the fast listing to full-read parity on Workdir across writer-written/reformatted/resumed shapes. Bite-checked both layers: reverting the workdir filter in unfinishedRunOf fails the cmd test ('continued "20260822-010000", want this project's run'); removing the scanEntry lift fails both listing tests; restored, all pass. Gate green afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, full make test, make race, make cover-check at 91.7% (threshold 90%).

grievance: The documented way to point a command at a non-default configuration - a global flag ahead of the command word - silently lost the two flags `new` cares about most. The subcommand walk parsed whatever sat ahead of `new`/`sessions`/`config`, but the forwarding table it feeds listed only --model, --dir and --orders-dir, even though --config and --provider were already being passed to it: `zot --config ~/zot.yaml new --draft "the objective"` and `zot --provider p new --draft "..."` therefore ran their drafting survey through whatever the DEFAULT resolution found - on a bare host an outright failure (`zot: provider "zai": provider: no API key configured`, exit 1), and on a host with a working default config something worse than failure: the survey billed whichever provider and model that config names, not the one the operator named. The `config` command fared no better, and it takes no flags of its own to escape with: `zot --config X config` opened the default file in $EDITOR while the operator believed they were editing X, and `zot --config X config path` printed the default path. docs/configuration.md promises the opposite of all three ('Commands accept global flags ahead of them, so a non-default config travels with any of them'), and the layering it documents (defaults < file < env < flags) was quietly inverted for exactly this spelling.
change: The forwarding table now lists all five globals `new` speaks: --config and --provider travel with the word like the rest. The `config` subcommand resolves its file from --config first - editConfig takes the path, empty still meaning the default location - so `zot --config X config` seeds and opens X and `zot --config X config path` prints X; with no flag given, ZOT_CONFIG answers as before, and the flag beats the environment exactly as it does for the run the config would drive. One deliberate consequence: a flag `new` refuses without --draft (--provider, --model) is now refused wherever on the line it sits, because it actually arrives - previously the refusal fired only when the flag followed the word, so the same mistake vanished or failed depending on word order.
proof: Live against the rebuilt release binary with a local OpenAI-compatible stub named by /tmp/zstub/config.yaml (provider local -> http://127.0.0.1:8099/v1, model test-model). Before: `zot --config /tmp/zstub/config.yaml new --draft "add rate limiting to the API"` died with `zot: provider "zai": provider: no API key configured` (exit 1). After: the survey runs - the stub's access log shows two POSTs to /v1/chat/completions carrying model=test-model - and the order lands with drafted acceptance criteria (- the suite passes), exit 0. `zot --config X --provider local new --draft ...` behaves identically, and `zot --provider some-provider new "an objective"` is now refused (`--provider and --model configure the drafting survey; add --draft to run one`) where the pre-shift binary scaffolded an order while ignoring the provider. `zot --config /tmp/zstub/config.yaml config path` prints the named path; `VISUAL=true zot --config /tmp/named-config.yaml config` seeds it from the template ('Created /tmp/named-config.yaml from the template.') and opens it; bare `zot config path` still prints the default (/home/runner/.config/zot/config.yaml). No earlier pass regressed: ./zot --help exits 0 with the full usage on stdout and zero bytes on stderr, an order run end to end settles with the digest block (session id, resume line, token totals), and `zot sessions` keeps the length/cost columns and outcome quoting of shifts 3 and 5. Tests added (cmd/zot/main_test.go): TestADraftRunsThroughTheConfigNamedAheadOfTheCommandWord drives run() with a good config behind --config and a 500-ing one behind ZOT_CONFIG, so the drafted criteria in the file prove which configuration served the survey - and the flag-beats-env layering is pinned too; TestAProviderAheadOfNewIsRefusedWithoutDraft asserts the position-independent refusal and that nothing scaffolds; TestTheConfigCommandOpensTheConfigNamedAheadOfIt and TestConfigPathHonoursTheFlagAheadOfTheCommandWord cover the config command both ways. Bite-checked by reverting the two code hunks while keeping the tests: the draft test fails through the wrong (500) server, the refusal test fails with err == nil, the open test fails on the missing named file, and the path test prints the env's path instead of the named one; restored, all four pass and the full suite stays green. Gate afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, make test, make race clean, make cover-check at 91.7% (threshold 90%).

grievance: The flags reference - docs/configuration.md, the page an operator consults to drive the tool - was broken twice over. A duplicated `--dir` row sat above blank lines that split the markdown table in two, and a markdown table split by a blank line stops being a table: rendered against the pre-shift page, mistune produced one 3-row table where the section declares 16 rows, so everything from `--max-iterations` down printed as raw pipe-delimited text. And half the flags were missing even as source: of the eighteen globals ./zot takes, the table named ten - `--rerun` and `--fresh`, the two ledger overrides the whole book loop turns on, were absent entirely (`--fresh` documented nowhere outside --help), as were `--color`, `-h`/`--help` and `--version`. The same drift had reached the other half of an operator's setup: configuration.md points at configs/zot.example.yaml as the reference where 'every field is documented', yet shift 4's `responses:` tri-state - which decides which API a custom endpoint speaks - appeared nowhere in it, and that template is not just documentation but what `zot config` seeds on first run.
change: The Flags section is now one well-formed GFM table naming all eighteen globals exactly once - the duplicate row and its blank lines are gone, the five missing flags are in (`--rerun` phrased as what a standing order runs under, `--fresh` as the escape from an automatic continuation), and effects keep to the flags' own help wording. configs/zot.example.yaml documents `responses:` beside the custom-gateway example where an operator types a base_url - the exact moment the choice matters - as commented YAML, so the seeded file still parses identically. Two drift guards now hold both references to the binary: TestTheFlagsReferenceListsEveryFlagExactlyOnce registers the globals the way a real invocation does and fails if any flag is missing from the table, listed on more than one row, stale, or split off by a blank line; TestTheSeededTemplateNamesEveryProviderField reflects over config.ProviderConfig's yaml tags and fails for any field the seeded template never names.
proof: Rendered before/after with mistune over the Flags section: pre-shift page -> 1 table, 3 <tr> (the rest plain text); post-shift -> 1 table, 16 <tr> = header plus every data row. ./zot --help rebuilt from release and dev tags lists 18 flag spellings that map 1:1 onto the table's rows (--color --config --diff --dir --fresh -h --max-iterations --model --no-session --orders-dir --plain --provider --records-dir --rerun --resume --session-dir --version --watch). Bite-checked both guards against the pre-fix files: TestTheFlagsReferenceListsEveryFlagExactlyOnce fails first on the blank-line split ('everything below the gap renders as plain text'), and with the split repaired but rows removed fails on 'flags ... never lists ... fresh, help, rerun'; TestTheSeededTemplateNamesEveryProviderField fails with 'configs/zot.example.yaml never mentions "responses:"'. Restored, all pass. Live: env HOME=/tmp/... VISUAL=true zot config seeds a fresh config whose line 252 carries '#   responses: false'; and an order run against the local stub provider still settles end to end ('status done', session/resume lines, token totals) with `zot sessions` showing the shifts-3/5 columns unchanged. Gate afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, full make test, make race clean, make cover-check at 91.7% (threshold 90%).

grievance: The first thing zot said to someone who had not written an order yet was the complete usage manual. A bare `zot` in a project with no orders - the most common first contact there is, and the state every new project starts in - dumped the full ~4,900-byte help block on stderr (usage, examples, book philosophy, watch-mode docs, all eighteen flags) before ending with its actual answer: `no order given, and <dir> holds none (write one with ...)` - 102 bytes buried at the very bottom of a hundred lines of flags for a tool the person is still meeting. The teaching intent was right; the delivery buried the lesson under reference material nobody asked for. Worse, the message conflated two different empties: an orders directory that does not exist yet read exactly like one that exists and holds no orders, so a `--dir` pointed at the wrong project was indistinguishable from a project awaiting its first order. Shift 1 made help answer when asked for; this path printed it unasked.
change: listOrdersRoot answers in one sentence and prints nothing: the error names what was looked at (the resolved orders root), gives the next step (`write one with zot new "the objective"`, then run zot again), and points at --help for everything else - which still prints in full on stdout when asked for, and on stderr from the genuine misuse paths (unknown flag, parse error) exactly as before. The sentence also distinguishes the two empties: `there is no orders directory at <root> yet` versus `<root> holds no orders`, so a misdirected --dir announces itself.
proof: Rebuilt release binary, bare `zot` in a fresh project: before the change stderr carried 4,960 bytes ending in the 102-byte actionable line (observed pre-shift); after, stderr is exactly 167 bytes - the single line `zot: no order given, and there is no orders directory at /tmp/proof9/.zot/orders yet - write one with \`zot new "the objective"\`, then run zot again (--help says more)` - stdout stays empty, exit stays 1. With `.zot/orders` created but empty the same invocation reads `... /tmp/proof9/.zot/orders holds no orders - ...`, naming the second empty correctly. Nothing else moved: `./zot --help` still exits 0 with all 4,858 bytes on stdout and zero on stderr; a non-empty book still announces `running 1 order(s) from <root>`, runs against the stub provider, records the receipt, and the next bare zot reports `already satisfied by run <id>` as before; `--dir /tmp/otherbook` shows the missing-directory wording for a wrong-project pointer. Tests (cmd/zot/main_test.go): TestAnEmptyBookAnswersWithAPointerNotTheManual drives run() end to end and holds both halves - the error must name the root, point at `zot new` and `--help`, and stderr must carry zero bytes (the old code failed it with the whole manual); TestAnEmptyBookSaysWhichKindOfEmptyItIs pins the missing-vs-existing wording through listOrdersRoot directly. Bite-checked by reverting the main.go hunk while keeping the tests: both fail (stderr wall returns; words say `holds none`), restored they pass, full suite green. Gate afterwards: make vet over release and dev builds, make test, make race clean, make cover-check at 91.7% (threshold 90%).
